title: The Neighbour, ricercar a 4 - string quartet (Beethoven: Grosse Fuge / Op. 131)
comment: The interpretation (tempo, rubato, dynamics, roles) is the Beethoven piano version's (plan.json). Solo string quartet, one player per voice: soprano vn1, alto vn2, tenor va, bass vc. The alto's lament countersubject (CS1, 9:4-12:4) dips to F3 and G-flat3, below violin II's G3, while the tenor still rests, so the viola plays it and hands it back to violin II at 13:1, where the viola itself enters with the tenor's answer (BLUEPRINT section 8); the viola's first lament note (F3 on its C string, 9:4-10:1) is +0.6 so the violin-to-viola seam does not dip (+0.3 left it 2.8 dB under violin II's last note), and orchestrate.py lifts the alto's F3 at 12:4 60 ms before the tenor's F3 on the same key at 13:1. Balance where register masks an entry: violin II +0.3 level for the answer (5:1), the viola +0.6 for the tenor's answer in its low register (13:1-17:4) over the cello's lament -0.2 (13:4-17:3), in the combination violin II +0.4 for S2 (48:1-50:3), then violin II and viola -0.3 (50:3-52:1) so the soprano's diminution heads lead the three speeds, as in the piano version, while the cello's augmentation (cf) gives -0.5 (48:1-50:3) and -0.8 (50:3-52:1). Climax I stays below Climax II (the plan's ff- against fff): all four parts -0.5 over the liquidation's peak (26:3-29:1; -0.4 left Climax II only 2.05 LU above it in 3 s loudness), but not on the fermata chord at 29:1, which starts at CC 101 and would drop into the mf layer; at Climax II (52:1-54:1), where the violins reach the CC ceiling, the viola -0.3 and the cello -0.7 (still in its ff layer) so the alto's diminution heads come through. Sforzando bite (velocity +12) at Climax I (28:1-30:1) and Climax II (52:1-54:1). The cello's re-struck tonic pedal in the coda (63:1-end) +0.5 so its tolling is heard under the tenor's head and the held d''. Articulation: the renderer infers per note with --short-ms 480 (render_args): eighths and sixteenths faster than 60 bpm get its short stroke, quarters and longer notes are slurred or new-bowed as the line connects. Hints (CC20): the arioso's pulsing eighths in violin II and viola (30:1-35:1) are detache (CC20 32, a new bow on every eighth; inferred, the repeated pitches re-bowed with a dip and the changes slurred, which limped); the cello's first inversion head at 35:4 (0.48 s eighths at 60 bpm, astride the 480 ms line) is short like every later head. A hinted part carries CC20 on every note; bowing.py (render.sh) gives its auto notes the renderer's own inference at 480 ms (orchestrate.py infers them at the renderer's default 260). Breaths: bowing.py ends the notes sounding into the breaths at 30:1 (the general pause after the fermata chord: 1.5 s), 35:1 (0.5 s of its 0.7) and 46:1 (0.3 s of its 0.35) and tapers their envelope 2 levels over their last 0.3 s, as the players lift their bows (perform.py lengthens those notes by the breath, which the piano's decay hides and a bow does not). Swells on long notes: perform.py's own 0.45-level swell on every note of a half or longer, deepened by swell.py after orchestrate.py (see render.sh) by 0.75 level at mf and softer, 0.375 at f and none at ff and louder, where the players hold a full bow; not on the notes starting in 61:3-63:1, where all four hold the C7 chord inside the diminuendo after the tune's peak. Positions are section marks from design/final-lab/piece.py.
